en.titre:
10/10 hobbies that actually
work if you have adhd

en.accroche: every wall is a _puzzle_ for your _whole body_
colonne: a route takes a few minutes, you fall, you try again, so a brain that gets bored fast always has a _next attempt_
en.chute: most gyms rent shoes and run an intro session

en.accroche: no one to keep up with, so you _actually look_
colonne: skip the rooms you don't care about and stand in front of one painting until you find something new in it
_pro tip_: artura gives me one painting a day and the story behind it, in a few minutes
en.chute: pick one room, one hour, then leave

en.accroche: the clay falls apart the _second_ you _drift_
colonne: your hands are covered in clay so the phone can't win, and the wheel gives you _instant feedback_ on every move
en.chute: look for a one-night wheel class near you

en.accroche: new ground _every step_, so you _can't zone out_
colonne: roots, rocks and hills keep giving your brain something new to read, and a race date gives it a _real goal_
_pro tip_: atala builds my runs around my goal and adjusts them every week
en.chute: start with a flat park trail, walk the hills

en.accroche: you use _both hands_ and _both feet_ at once
colonne: keeping four limbs on one beat leaves no room for a wandering thought, and you hear right away when you're _off_
en.chute: a practice pad and a metronome are enough
